what_its_for: Tamoxifen is used to treat and help prevent certain types of breast cancer in both women and men. It works by blocking the effects of estrogen (a natural hormone) on breast tissue, which can slow or stop the growth of some breast cancer cells. Your doctor may also prescribe it to lower the risk of breast cancer if you are at high risk.
how_to_take: Take tamoxifen by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablets. If you are using the liquid form (Soltamox), measure your dose carefully with the measuring device provided — do not use a regular kitchen spoon.
dosing: The most common dose for adults is 20 mg once a day, or 10 mg twice a day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. Treatment usually lasts 5 to 10 years depending on your situation. Always follow your doctor's instructions and do not change your dose without talking to them first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once or extra doses to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store tamoxifen tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid form (Soltamox) at room temperature and use it within 3 months of opening. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant while taking tamoxifen, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable non-hormonal birth control (such as condoms or a copper IUD) during treatment and for at least 2 months after your last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it may interfere with the medication. Do not take hormonal therapies like estrogen products or birth control pills without talking to your doctor first. Avoid smoking, as it may reduce the effectiveness of the drug. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, especially antidepressants like fluoxetine or paroxetine, as they can reduce how well tamoxifen works.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: unusual vaginal bleeding or discharge, pelvic pain or pressure, sudden leg pain, swelling, or redness in your legs (possible blood clot), sudden chest pain or shortness of breath, vision changes or blurred vision, severe headache or dizziness, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), signs of stroke such as sudden numbness or weakness on one side, slurred speech, or confusion, or new lumps or changes in your breast. Also call your doctor if you have mood changes, hot flashes that are very bothersome, or any other side effects that worry you.
when_it_works: Tamoxifen does not work overnight. For breast cancer treatment, it may take several weeks to months before you notice benefits, and it works best when taken consistently over the long term (often 5 to 10 years). For cancer prevention, the benefit may continue even after you stop taking it. Do not stop taking tamoxifen without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take tamoxifen if you are pregnant. It can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Use effective non-hormonal birth control during treatment and for at least 2 months after stopping. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking tamoxifen. Older adults: Older patients may have a higher risk of blood clots and stroke — discuss your personal risk with your doctor. Liver problems: Your doctor may need to monitor your liver function or adjust your dose if you have liver disease. Premenopausal women: This medicine may affect your menstrual cycle and fertility. Talk to your doctor if you plan to become pregnant in the future.
